text:
anya: Heads-up — noticed a sharp increase in prefix-cache misses after the recent system-prompt tweak. Hit-rate down ~18% for chat-v1 on prod during the 09:00–10:00 ramp. Profiling attached below. :eyes:

mike: Ugh. Which piece of the key changed? We include model+prompt+toolmeta hash right now, right?

sriram: We landed a system prompt edit (trailing newline + a small function metadata block) and also reordered tool metadata when a tool has no schema. That ordering change will mutate the canonical JSON string we hash.

anya: Right. Current key = sha1(model + '|' + prompt_raw + '|' + json.dumps(tool_meta)). No normalization. Example of spike from logs:
```
2026-03-15T09:12:03Z prefix_cache MISS key=sha1:8f3a... model=chat-v1 user=svc-frontend prefix_len=34
2026-03-15T09:12:04Z prefix_cache MISS key=sha1:7b2c... model=chat-v1 user=svc-frontend prefix_len=34
```

julia: Two vectors to fix: 1) canonicalize tool/function fields (sort keys, stable stringify) 2) pin tokenizer/version in key so tokenization drift doesn't fragment cache. We've seen subtle tokenizer patches change token boundaries and bust warmups.

prefetch-bot: warmup-summary: prefetch hit_rate baseline=0.86, this morning=0.70, warmup_misses increased x3 for new instances.

mike: Quick experiment — I pushed a tiny canary that does: canonical_tools_json = json.dumps(tool_meta, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':')) and key includes tokenizer_id. Simulated traffic locally with fuzzed tool ordering and misses dropped to ~2.4% (from 18).

anya: Great signal. Two concerns: sorting on hot path adds CPU; also customers sometimes vary system prompt per tenant which could increase key cardinality. We need a strategy that balances CPU vs fragmentation.

sriram: Proposal: introduce cache_key versioning + lightweight fast path. Algorithm: if prefix_token_count < 40 -> fast_key = sha1(model + '|' + tokenizer_id + '|' + raw_prefix_bytes). Else -> stable_key = sha1(model + '|' + tokenizer_id + '|' + normalize_ws(system_prompt) + '|' + canonical_tool_key). Also store key_version header with requests so we can roll.

julia: normalize_ws = collapse consecutive whitespace to single space, trim, and remove trailing newline; canonical_tool_key = sha1(sorted_tool_kv_bytes) where we flatten tool list into [(name, sorted(kv))...] to keep deterministic order. Add a new request header `X-Cache-Key-Version` when a tenant explicitly sets system_prompt_version. If absent we infer default 'v1' to preserve old keys.

mike: I'll open PR for canonical_tool_key and tokenizer_pin. Also add metric tag `cache.key_version` and `cache.key_type=fast|stable` so we can monitor. Will run microbench on canary.

anya: For warmup/backfill: update prefetch worker to emit both fast_key and stable_key for a short window so newly spawned replicas populate both namespaces. Also add regression alert if fast_key hit_rate drops >5% vs baseline.

sriram: Edge-case: tools with user-supplied freeform JSON in a arg break deterministic sorting because keys may be nested. For now treat tool.args as opaque string and include a tool_schema_version if available.

julia: Good call. Also add tokenizer_version pin per model in the model registry UI so ops can lock a model to a tokenizer when we do risky tokenizer patches.

mike: Local perf numbers: stable_key construction ~+120ns per request in optimized C path; Python layer prototype was ~+1.1µs. Looks acceptable.

anya: Nice. Let's AB test: route 5% of traffic to key_v2 (stable+token-pin) for 24h on canary region, collect hit-rate, cold-start latency, and CPU. If safe, ramp to 25% then full roll. I'll coordinate with eng-sre for the rollout windows. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy started — canary/key-v2 -> cluster-canary-3 (deploy id: dpl-20260315-089)

mike: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/4827 (draft) — contains canonicalization + metrics + header.

anya: Thanks. Follow-ups: 1) add backfill job to prefetch (both keys) 2) update model registry with tokenizer pin UI 3) document key_versioning in ops runbook. I'll file tickets and assign.

sriram: One last optimization idea: memoize canonical_tool_key per request if multiple prefixes share same tool_meta (e.g., different user messages in same session). That reduces repeated sorts.

julia: Agreed. Also add integration test to fuzz tool ordering and system prompt whitespace.

anya: Sounds good. I'll post retrospective with hit-rate graphs after the canary run. :spiral_calendar:
